children: , the global insurance-brokerage and risk-advisory company, slid approximately 7.0% to $330.52 Monday after unveiling its $17 billion acquisition of USI Insurance Services. The deal gives Aon a much larger foothold in the U.S. middle-market and excess-and-surplus insurance businesses, but investors immediately focused on the price tag and heavier debt load.

USI brings approximately $3 billion in annual revenue, valuing the transaction at roughly 5.7 times sales. Aon plans to finance the purchase with debt, pause near-term share repurchases and prioritize repayment after the expected fourth-quarter closing. Management forecasts an adjusted earnings boost beginning in 2028, leaving shareholders to absorb the financing pressure well before the promised payoff arrives.

Aon reported $4.2 billion of second-quarter revenue, while the USI deal pushes its combined middle-market acquisition spending with NFP to approximately $30 billion. The stock's $330.52 price now sits 15.81% below its $392.61 GF Value, signaling that the market has already imposed a steep execution discount. Aon is buying scale aggressively; Monday's plunge shows investors want faster evidence that integration, leverage reduction and earnings growth can justify the bill.

title: Aon Sinks 6.6% as $17 Billion Deal Freezes Buybacks
